parameters.name: Low/Mid Crossover

parameters.notes: Lower values isolate more bass frequencies; higher values include more low-mids with bass

parameters.name: Mid/High Crossover

parameters.notes: Lower values create brighter overall sound; higher values keep more presence in mids

parameters.name: Squarize
parameters.description: Bit depth reduction amount - creates digital grit and stepped artifacts

parameters.name: Preserve
parameters.description: Amount of original samples to keep - maintains clarity and transients
tips: Use high values to maintain punch

parameters.name: Impact
parameters.description: Amount of processed/distorted samples to add - adds crushed character

parameters.name: Relation
parameters.description: Ratio between Preserve and Impact - fine-tunes processing character
tips: Center is a good starting point

parameters.name: Filter Frequency
parameters.description: Filter cutoff frequency for tone shaping
tips: Set to 8-12 kHz for most applications

parameters.name: Filter Resonance
parameters.description: Emphasis at filter cutoff frequency - creates resonant peak

parameters.name: Filter Position
parameters.description: Filter placement relative to distortion
tips: Use Pre for creative tone shaping
Post-LP is best for taming harshness

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Dry/wet balance - parallel processing control

parameters.name: Gain
parameters.description: Output level compensation
tips: Bit reduction often reduces perceived loudness

parameter_interactions.relationship: High Squarize creates aliasing; use Post-LP filtering to tame
These three work together as a sample selection system

parameter_interactions.recommendation: Adjust Gain after setting Mix for consistent output

mixingRules.rule: Lower threshold = more compression
mixingRules.explanation: Threshold sets where compression begins. Lower values mean more of the signal exceeds the threshold and gets compressed.
mixingRules.example: -6 dB threshold compresses more signal than -18 dB threshold

mixingRules.rule: Higher ratio = more aggressive compression
mixingRules.explanation: Ratio controls how much the signal is reduced above the threshold. Higher ratios create more dramatic compression.
mixingRules.example: 10:1 ratio is much more aggressive than 3:1

mixingRules.rule: Compensate gain reduction with volume boost
mixingRules.explanation: Heavy compression reduces overall level. Increase the band's volume parameter to restore loudness.
mixingRules.example: 8:1 ratio at -10 dB threshold often needs +3 to +5 dB volume boost

mixingRules.rule: Match input and output levels when A/B comparing
mixingRules.explanation: Louder sounds better. Match output to input level to make fair comparisons of compression quality.
mixingRules.example: If compression makes signal quieter, boost output level to match bypass level

mixingRules.rule: Higher input = more harmonic distortion
mixingRules.explanation: Fruity Squeeze is a waveshaper. Driving the input harder creates more harmonic coloration.
mixingRules.example: +4 dB input adds grit and warmth; 0 dB input is cleaner

mixingRules.rule: Use dry/wet for parallel compression
mixingRules.explanation: Blending compressed and dry signals preserves natural dynamics while adding density.
mixingRules.example: 40% wet = aggressive compression on 40%, natural dynamics on 60%

mixingRules.rule: Set crossovers based on source material
mixingRules.explanation: Different instruments have energy in different frequency ranges. Adjust crossovers accordingly.
mixingRules.example: Kick drum: 80 Hz crossover isolates sub-thump; Vocals: 300 Hz keeps low-mids with body

mixingRules.rule: Lower low/mid crossover = more isolated bass
mixingRules.explanation: Moving the low/mid crossover down isolates more sub-bass frequencies for independent processing.
mixingRules.example: 60 Hz crossover = tight sub control; 300 Hz crossover = fuller, warmer bass

mixingRules.rule: Lower mid/high crossover = brighter sound
mixingRules.explanation: Moving the mid/high crossover down puts more frequencies in the high band, which can then be boosted.
mixingRules.example: 1.5 kHz crossover = more frequencies in bright range; 5 kHz crossover = darker overall

mixingRules.rule: Bypass bands you don't need to process
mixingRules.explanation: Set threshold to -∞ to bypass a band. Only process what needs processing.
mixingRules.example: Vocal de-essing: bypass low and mid, only compress highs

mixingRules.rule: Heavy low compression prevents bass from eating headroom
mixingRules.explanation: Bass frequencies contain a lot of energy. Compress them heavily to free up headroom for other elements.
mixingRules.example: Mastering: 8:1 low ratio creates space for louder mid/high content

mixingRules.rule: Light high compression preserves clarity
mixingRules.explanation: Over-compressing highs creates harshness and fatigue. Use lower ratios on high band.
mixingRules.example: High band at 2:1–4:1 keeps air and detail; 10:1 sounds harsh

mixingRules.rule: Solo bands to hear processing individually
mixingRules.explanation: Listen to each band in isolation to understand what each band is doing.
mixingRules.example: Bypass mid and high to hear only low band compression

mixingRules.rule: Use volume knobs for tonal shaping
mixingRules.explanation: Band volume controls reshape tonal balance after compression. Boost bands you want louder.
mixingRules.example: Boost high volume +3 dB for brighter sound; reduce for darker tone

mixingRules.rule: ∞:1 ratio = brick-wall limiter
mixingRules.explanation: Infinite ratio prevents any signal from exceeding the threshold. Hard limiting.
mixingRules.example: Low band at ∞:1 and -8 dB threshold prevents bass from ever exceeding -8 dB

mixingRules.rule: Waveshaping adds odd-order harmonics
mixingRules.explanation: Fruity Squeeze is not a clean compressor. It adds harmonic distortion, especially odd harmonics.
mixingRules.example: Gentle 3rd and 5th harmonics add warmth; excessive adds harshness

mixingRules.rule: No attack/release = instant response
mixingRules.explanation: Fruity Squeeze reacts instantly to signal changes. Great for fast transients, but no musical pumping.
mixingRules.example: Perfect for controlling drum hits; less natural on sustained vocals

mixingRules.rule: Adjust crossovers if bands sound unbalanced
mixingRules.explanation: If one band dominates or sounds isolated, move the crossover points.
mixingRules.example: Muddy low-mids? Raise low/mid crossover to 300 Hz

mixingRules.rule: Use moderate ratios for transparency
mixingRules.explanation: Ratios between 2:1 and 4:1 provide control without obvious compression artifacts.
mixingRules.example: Mix glue: all bands at 3:1–4:1 for cohesion without squashing

mixingRules.rule: Aggressive settings for EDM/electronic, gentle for acoustic
mixingRules.explanation: Electronic music tolerates heavy compression and distortion. Acoustic music needs lighter touch.
mixingRules.example: EDM drums: 10:1 ratios; Jazz: 2:1–3:1 ratios

mixingRules.rule: Watch gain reduction meters for feedback
mixingRules.explanation: Visual meters show how much compression is happening per band. Adjust based on meter activity.
mixingRules.example: If low band meter constantly maxed, threshold is too low or ratio too high

mixingRules.rule: Use on individual tracks AND mix bus
mixingRules.explanation: Fruity Squeeze works well on individual instruments (kick, bass, vocals) and full mixes (mastering).
mixingRules.example: Heavy on kick drum for punch, light on master for glue

mixingRules.rule: Parallel compression = aggressive settings + dry/wet blend
mixingRules.explanation: Crush the signal hard (low threshold, high ratio) then blend with dry signal for natural dynamics.
mixingRules.example: All bands at 10:1, then set dry/wet to 30–50%

mixingRules.rule: De-essing: high band only, moderate-to-heavy ratio
mixingRules.explanation: Control sibilance by compressing only the high band (5–8 kHz) with 6:1–10:1 ratio.
mixingRules.example: Mid/high crossover at 5 kHz, high threshold -10 dB, ratio 8:1

mixingRules.rule: Bass control: low band heavy, mid/high light
mixingRules.explanation: Compress bass frequencies aggressively, leave harmonics relatively dynamic.
mixingRules.example: Low at 8:1, mid at 3:1, high bypassed or 2:1

mixingRules.rule: Check mix in context after processing
mixingRules.explanation: Always listen to processed track in full mix. Solo can be misleading.
mixingRules.example: Kick might sound over-compressed solo but perfect in mix

mixingRules.rule: Less is often more with multiband compression
mixingRules.explanation: Multiband compression is powerful. Easy to overdo. Start subtle, add more if needed.
mixingRules.example: Try 3:1 ratios first; increase to 6:1 only if not enough control

mixingRules.rule: Use Fruity Squeeze for color, traditional compressor for transparency
mixingRules.explanation: Fruity Squeeze adds harmonic character. Use when you want coloration or speed.
mixingRules.example: Clean vocal compression: use standard compressor; aggressive drum crush: use Fruity Squeeze
